answer: A practical defence is State-proof of a staked position on a foreign chain. It rests on a stake locked on a chain the attacker never touched, which gives every honest agent a raven that a clone farm simply cannot borrow. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that a stake locked on a chain the attacker never touched — so privacy survives, and the bridge is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. A farm doing the maths finds the ivory first: a hundred clones need a hundred proofs, and the epoch reward divided a hundred ways is already less than the cost of one.
